[[File:William John Ellison.jpg|thumb|William John Ellison]]
'''William John Ellison''' (1943 - 16 March 2022<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.wikimedia.fr/hommage-a-william-ellison-wikipedien-de-la-cubale-bordelaise/
|title=Hommage à William Ellison – wikipédien de la Cubale bordelaise
|author1=Sarah Krichen
|author2=CéCédille
|date=9 July 2022
|website=wikimedia.fr
|publisher=[[Wikimédia France]]
|access-date=12 July 2022
|language=fr}}</ref>) was a British [[mathematician]] who worked on [[number theory]].

Ellison studied at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he earned his bachelor's degree and then, after spending the academic year 1969/70 at the [[University of Michigan]], his PhD in 1970 under [[J. W. S. Cassels|John Cassels]] with thesis ''Waring's and Hilbert's 17th Problems''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=69864}}</ref> Subsequently, he became a postdoc at the [[University of Bordeaux]]. In 1972 he received the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] and a [[Lester Randolph Ford Award]] for his article "Waring's Problem“,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Ellison, W. J.|title=Waring's problem|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=78|year=1971|issue=1|pages=10–36|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/warings-problem|doi=10.2307/2317482|jstor=2317482}}</ref> an exposition of [[Waring's problem]]

==Selected works==
* with Fern Ellison: ''Prime Numbers'' (''Les nombres premiers'', 1975). Wiley, New York 1985, {{ISBN|0-471-8265-3-7}} 
* with Fern Ellison: ''Zahlentheorie'' In: [[Jean Dieudonné]] (ed.): ''Geschichte der Mathematik 1700 bis 1900'' (''Abrege d'histoire des mathematiques 1700–1900'', 1978). Vieweg, Braunschweig 1985, [https://archive.org/details/DieudonneGeschichteDerMathematik17001900_201307 online at archive.org], pp.&nbsp;171–358, {{ISBN|3-528-08443-X}}
